thread:
Sam W: Heads-up — nightly perf suite showed a tail-latency regression after the FP8 kernel merge. 95p latency up ~18% on long sequences :confused:
perf-bot: nightly-run-1790123400: perf-regression detected: windows/95p_token_latency +18% (p<0.01). Full report: https://perf/reports/1790123400
Anya P: Ugh. Any idea whether it's kernel selection or batching changes?
Kevin L: Dumped grpc profiling + kernel-choice counters for a few requests. Looks like for long sequences we're selecting the new fp8_mixed kernel more often (expected), but calibration_passes counter spikes per request. Snippet:
```
kernel_choice: fp8_mixed
calibration_passes: 3
kv_cache_writes: 1
batch_size_effective: 1
latency_ms: 320
```
Marta R: Calibration passes on hot path are a red flag. Were we doing on-the-fly per-request calibration when model first hits new kernel? I thought we only calibrate offline.
Sam W: The change in runtime defaults set `quant.calibration_mode=auto` in the merge — which runs live calibration for int8/fp8 when it sees new input distributions. That explains the extra work.
Anya P: Right — `auto` was meant for offline experiments. For production it should be `manual` or `none`. Can we make SDK default to `manual` while keeping `auto` as an explicit opt-in?
Kevin L: Agreed. Also batching heuristics interact badly: when calibration runs it forces batch_size_effective=1 for a bit. So throughput drops and latency spikes. We should expose a safety rail: `quantization.safety.preserve_batching=true` that prevents calibration from disabling batching.
Marta R: From docs POV we need to document three knobs: `quant.calibration_mode`, `quant.preset` (e.g., fast|balanced|safe), and `quant.safety.*` flags. Include recommended presets: safe -> no live calibration, force float fallback for attention; balanced -> offline calibration allowed; fast -> aggressive fp8 with auto-calibration.
docs-bot: draft doc ticket created: DOCS-987: "Quantization knobs and safety rails in SDK".
Sam W: Proposal for SDK API (python):
```
client = RedwoodClient(...)
resp = client.generate(
  model="rwd/fp8-7b",
  prompt="...",
  quantization={
    "preset":"balanced",
    "calibration_mode":"manual",   # none|auto|manual
    "safety": {"preserve_batching": true, "max_calibration_passes": 0}
  }
)
```
Kevin L: Suggest `max_calibration_passes` default=0 in hosted to avoid surprises. We can log any fallback to calibration in request metadata: `x-quant-calibration=triggered` and emit perf counter `calibration_passes`.
Anya P: Can we add a canary that turns on `auto` for 5% traffic and measures quality delta vs perf cost? That would give us data for balanced/default choice.
Marta R: Yes — also add a docs section: "When to use live calibration" with example telemetry queries and how to set `presets` for production. Include a compatibility matrix for fp8/int8/4bit kernels and model families.
Sam W: Action items:
- Kevin: change runtime default to `manual` and add `preserve_batching` safety rail (small patch) — target: today.
- Marta/docs: write DOCS-987 with examples and recommended presets + migration notes — target: EOD tomorrow.
- Anya: create perf canary config (5% traffic, measure quality/regression) — target: next week.
- perf-bot: include `calibration_passes` in nightly perf report and flag changes >1 as warning.
perf-bot: noted. I will include calibration_passes and kernel_choice in the next run.
Kevin L: One more note — KV cache behavior: when calibration runs we currently evict a small proportion of KV cache to free memory for calibration buffers. That increases repeated token compute for long-conversation flows. Add `quant.safety.preserve_kv_cache=true` option to opt out.
Anya P: Good catch. Make that default for Dedicated/Private deployments. Hosted can be `false` but clearly documented.
Marta R: I'll add a small FAQ explaining the latency vs quality tradeoffs and a quick checklist for prod: disable `auto`, enable `preserve_batching` and `preserve_kv_cache`, or use `preset:safe` for customer-facing flows.
Sam W: Cool. If we land the runtime default + SDK param change then we can roll out with a docs note and avoid customer incidents. :thumbsup:
Marta R: I'll link the doc once created.
Kevin L: I'll open PR for the runtime change and reference DOCS-987.
Anya P: Thanks all — keeping this thread for visibility. Ping me when PRs merge.
Marta R: :eyes:
